podcast.title: Naked Urination on Vancouver Audience – October 31, 1993, Pacific Coliseum
podcast.body: On Halloween 1993, Blind Melon were supporting Lenny Kravitz at a sold-out Pacific Coliseum in Vancouver (13,000 people). Singer Shannon Hoon stripped naked for the final three songs, then urinated on the audience. The band attempted to escape on their tour bus, but police cruisers blocked the exit. Hoon climbed onto the roof of the bus and began screaming at the officers. It took 15 minutes to talk him down; he was then arrested and charged with committing an indecent act. The promoter spent the following weeks apologizing to those who had been urinated upon. "Which kind of gives a whole new meaning to the title of this song."

podcast.title: Extensive Touring Schedule (1995)
podcast.body: Blind Melon undertook tours with prominent artists such as Neil Young, Lenny Kravitz, and The Rolling Stones, indicative of their rising profile in the mid-1990s. This touring activity, however, also occurred during a period where frontman Shannon Hoon was struggling with severe drug and alcohol issues. "There were tours with Neil Young and Lenny Kravitz in the Rolling Stones."

podcast.title: Fatal Drug Binge (October 1995)
podcast.body: On October 20, 1995, after a problematic show at Numbers club in Houston, Shannon Hoon engaged in an all-night drug binge and had to be coerced onto the tour bus for the 350-mile drive to New Orleans. He continued using cocaine throughout the night on the bus and, immediately upon arrival in New Orleans, left to acquire more. Early on October 21st, he crept back to a bunk on the bus. Around noon, sound tech Lyle Eves found him unresponsive, and an ambulance was called, but it was too late. "Shannon had an all-night drug binge and eventually had to be corral for the tour bus ride to the next show in New Orleans." "He was unresponsive. An ambulance was called, but it was too late."

podcast.title: Shannon Hoon's Overdose Death (1995)
podcast.body: Lead singer Shannon Hoon died on October 21, 1995, from a massive cocaine overdose on the band's tour bus. The bus was parked in a parking lot outside the Hotel Intercontinental in downtown New Orleans. The night before, Blind Melon had played a "bad show" in Houston, with Hoon "buzzed on Coke" for most of the gig, and he continued using his stash on the bus to New Orleans. He was last seen around 10 AM after having breakfast, before creeping back into guitarist Christopher Thorne's bunk, where he was found unresponsive shortly after noon. "The official coroner's verdict? Heart failure brought about by a massive cocaine overdose. The date was October 21, 1995."

podcast.title: "Bee Girl" Video Success
podcast.body: Samuel Bayer was hired to direct the music video for a single from their self-titled debut album. He cast his younger sister in the video, dressed in a bumblebee outfit, and the resulting "Bee Girl" video was a "smash," leading to the album selling "like crazy" and the band being taken seriously. "A dude named Samuel Beyer was hired to direct the video for a single from this self-titled debut album. He cast his little sister in the video and had her wear this bumblebee outfit. The video was a smash and the album started telling me like crazy."

podcast.title: Band Name Origin
podcast.body: The name "Blind Melon" was chosen either from a Cheech and Chong skit or from a term guitarist Roger Smith's father used to describe neighborhood stoners. "Blind Millen was chosen as their name, from either a Cheach and Chong Skip, or from a term guitarist Roger Smith's father used for neighborhood stoners."

podcast.title: Connection to Guns n' Roses
podcast.body: Shannon Hoon's sister was friends with Axl Rose during high school in Indiana, which led to Shannon singing backup vocals on a couple of Guns n' Roses songs and appearing in the "Don't Cry" video. "Shannon ended up in the Guns and Roses orbit because his sister had been friends with Axel Rose back in high school in Indiana."

podcast.title: Distinct Musical Identity
podcast.body: The band gained attention in the early 1990s because their sound was distinct and set them apart. They were explicitly "not part of the whole grunge thing" and "certainly not very punk," instead offering a "fresh reinvention of some classic rock moves in the vein of the grateful dead and Leonard Skinnerd." "They were definitely not part of the whole grunge thing, and they were certainly not very punk. Their sound was a fresh reinvention of some classic rock moves in the vein of the grateful dead and Leonard Skinnerd, and it really made them stand out from the crowd."

xref.title: Death by Cocaine Overdose (October 21, 1995)
xref.body: Shannon Hoon died on October 21, 1995, at the age of 28, from a heart attack brought on by a cocaine overdose. Despite Blind Melon's debut album going platinum four times over and a hit single, Shannon struggled with drug and alcohol issues, attempting rehab at least twice without success, against the advice of his drug counselor. The band had just finished recording their second album, "Soup," and had begun an 18-month tour on September 19, 1995. Following a disappointing show in Houston on October 20, Shannon went on an all-night drug binge. The band arrived in New Orleans early on October 21 to play Tipitina's. Shannon called his girlfriend for 45 minutes, explaining how "messed up" he was, then visited Smoothie King on Canal Street and spent 45 minutes talking to someone on a psychic hotline. He went back to the tour bus instead of the hotel, laid down in bandmate Christopher Thorn's bunk, and was found unresponsive by a sound technician at 1:30 PM. EMS declared him dead. "He was twenty-eight. He's buried in Dayton Cemetery in Dayton, Indiana, and the epitaph is from a blind million song called Change."

He made at least two attempts at rehab, facilitated by the band's manager, but nothing seemed to stick. "But Shannon was having issues with drugs in alcohol. xref.title: Final Hours in New Orleans (October 21, 1995)
xref.body: After an all-night drug binge following a disappointing Houston show, Shannon Hoon arrived in New Orleans with Blind Melon early on October 21, 1995, to play a club show at Tipitina's. While the rest of the group checked into a hotel, Shannon chose to go for a walk. He made a 45-minute call to his girlfriend, describing his "messed up" state, then visited a Smoothie King on Canal Street, and spent another 45 minutes talking on a psychic hotline. Instead of joining the band at the hotel, he returned to the tour bus, got undressed, and lay down in bandmate Christopher Thorn's bunk. He was found unresponsive at 1:30 PM by a sound technician attempting to wake him for sound check, and EMS declared him dead of a heart attack caused by a cocaine overdose. "While he was there, he apparently spent 45 minutes talking to somebody on a psychic hotline. When he hung up, he went back to the bus, instead of checking into the hotel with everybody else."

xref.title: Struggles with Addiction and Failed Rehab (Pre-1995)
xref.body: Shannon Hoon faced significant issues with drugs and alcohol, despite his band Blind Melon's success. He made at least two attempts at rehab, facilitated by the band's manager, but "nothing seemed to stick." His drug counselor explicitly advised against him embarking on an intensive 18-month tour, deeming him too fragile. A "reminder" (assigned person) was appointed to keep him clean on tour but was dismissed after only 28 gigs. "But Shannon was having issues with drugs in alcohol. xref.title: The "Soup" Album and Ill-Advised Tour (1995)
xref.body: Blind Melon managed to complete the recording of their second album, titled "Soup." Subsequently, on September 19, 1995, the band commenced a projected 18-month tour. This extensive touring schedule was undertaken specifically against the advice of Shannon Hoon's drug counselor, who felt that Shannon was "just too fragile to handle such an intense road trip." "The band did manage to get through the recording of their second album, which they called Soup. And then on September 19th of 1995, Blind Millen began a projected 18-month tour."
